summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, diastolic heart failure, and prior DVT/PE was admitted for worsening right lower extremity pain, erythema, and swelling with fever and leukocytosis. She was started on IV vancomycin and clindamycin for suspected cellulitis. After initial improvement, her infection worsened following transition to oral clindamycin, prompting re-initiation of IV vancomycin. Infectious disease recommended continuing IV therapy with aggressive edema management. Her swelling, attributed to lymphedema and heart failure, was managed with IV furosemide and bumetanide, with transition to oral diuretics. A low INR of 1.5 led to a thrombolytic dose via PICC and continued warfarin, though INR remained subtherapeutic at discharge (1.7). A positive C. difficile PCR without diarrhea was not treated. Pain was managed with oxycodone, morphine, and IV dilaudid, with recommendations for outpatient opioid weaning. She developed a non-infectious blister on the left calf. By discharge, infection had improved, and she was transitioned to oral doxycycline and cephalexin. She was discharged home with services, Narcan, and follow-up instructions for antibiotics, diuretics, INR monitoring, and PICC line evaluation.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Other epilepsy, not intractable, without status epilepticus
